name: Chamoline
lede: Chamoline is a dark orange-yellow from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary of color names, close to camel.

sections.title: A plate name from 1930
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* places Chamoline on plate 13, cell L8, with a first-recorded date of 1902 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed the same block of color as a dark orange yellow [2].

The same plate cell also carries the name Buckthorn Brown, first recorded in 1912 [1]. The dictionary gives no origin for either word, so the source of the name is undocumented here [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pinchbeck-brown]], [[dusty-bronze]], [[pinchbeck-brown]] and [[tawny-orange]], at 3.2, 3.4, 3.5 and 4.5 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this color in 1,657 of 23,781 paintings, about 7 percent, as photographed [4]. Bernardo Strozzi and Pietro Perugino carry it more than most painters in the set [4]. In our own [[ochre]]-to-[[tan]] range it reads as one of the darker, more orange members [4]. The match is computed from photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [4].
